function: RIS-aided hybrid beamforming: unrolled gradient projection with learned step sizes for jointly designing analog precoder, digital precoder and RIS phase shifts to maximize the achievable rate. p. 1-3
system: mmWave downlink: BS with N=64 antennas and Na=16 RF chains, K=10 single-antenna users, reflecting RIS (unit-modulus phase shifts) with 128 elements; carrier frequency not stated. p. 2, 3
method: Deep unfolding of gradient projection: layer-wise step sizes learned by gradient ascent on the achievable rate (unsupervised), Adam, PyTorch; 100 training channels, 30 epochs. p. 2-3
data_channel: Own simulator. Train: Rayleigh fading with path loss. Test: Rician fading with LoS as in the mmWave model of [1]; no 3GPP or measured channel. p. 3
test_conditions: Train: Rayleigh, N=64, K=10, NR=128, 130 dB power, 100 channels. Test (39 settings): Rician; N=32-256, K=1-16, NR=64-512, power 90-130 dB, user and RIS locations. p. 1, 3
baselines: Non-learned only: conventional gradient projection (GP) [8] and full-digital beamforming with RIS [16]; no learned baseline compared. p. 3, 4
metrics: Achievable rate versus users, antennas, RIS elements, power and locations; computation-time speedup over GP. p. 4
complexity: Order sum(Li)K^3 for unrolled GP (Li=5) versus sum(Ii)K^3 for GP (tens to hundreds of iterations); measured speedup about ten times. p. 3, 4
q1_support: p. 3: "the small scale channel is modelled to be Rayleigh fading channel"; test is Rician with LoS p. 3: "identical to the standard mmWave channel [1]" (a literature model, not a standardized one). Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 1: "Under a single training setting, the unrolled GP approach is tested under thirty nine different out-of-distribution settings"; p. 3: "the channels in training setting are different from that in the test setting" (Rayleigh to Rician, other N, K, NR, power, locations).
q3_support: p. 3: "The step size in the GP method and the full digital beamforming method is 0.5"; p. 4: "achievable rates of the unrolled GP method are larger than that of the GP method". Only non-learned GP [8] and full-digital beamforming with RIS [16] are compared; learned methods [18]-[20] appear only for training size (p. 3).
q4_support: p. 3: "the computational complexity of the unrolled GP method is" sum(Li)K^3, against sum(Ii)K^3 for GP; p. 4: "the computational times of the proposed unrolled GP method are ten times faster than the GP method" (measured, Figs. 2(d), 3(d)).
notes: Include, area 3: the learned step sizes drive the joint design of analog precoder, digital precoder and RIS phase shifts. q1 is 0 because the LoS part cites a literature mmWave model [1] (Sohrabi and Yu), not a standardized one; the reviewer may confirm. q3 is 0 because Figs. 2-3 show only GP [8] and full-digital beamforming with RIS [16], both non-learned. On p. 4 the paper states that a model trained in the high SNR region does not generalize well in the low SNR region.
